passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and proclaim this message there, saying, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, O king of Judah, who sits on the throne of David—you and your officials and your people who enter these gates.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD gives a command.
Go down to the palace of the king of Judah.
Speak this message there.
Say these words to the king of Judah.
The king of Judah sits on the throne of David.
You, king, must listen to the word of the LORD.
Your officials must listen.
Your people must listen.
All who enter these gates must listen.
passages.original: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה רֵ֖ד בֵּֽית־ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וְדִבַּרְתָּ֣ שָׁ֔ם אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה׃ וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב עַל־ כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֑ד אַתָּ֤ה וַעֲבָדֶ֙יךָ֙ וְעַמְּךָ֔ הַבָּאִ֖ים בַּשְּׁעָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: Administer justice and righteousness. Rescue the victim of robbery from the hand of his oppressor. Do no wrong or violence to the foreigner, the fatherless, or the widow. Do not shed innocent blood in this place.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the king of Judah and his people.
The LORD commands them to act with justice.
The LORD commands them to do what is right.
Rescue those who have been robbed.
Take them out of the hand of the oppressor.
Do not harm the foreigner.
Do not harm the fatherless.
Do not harm the widow.
Do not mistreat them.
Do not use violence against them.
Do not shed innocent blood in this place.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עֲשׂ֤וּ מִשְׁפָּט֙ וּצְדָקָ֔ה וְהַצִּ֥ילוּ גָז֖וּל מִיַּ֣ד עָשׁ֑וֹק וְגֵר֩ יָת֨וֹם וְאַלְמָנָ֤ה אַל־ תֹּנוּ֙ אַל־ תַּחְמֹ֔סוּ וְדָ֣ם נָקִ֔י אַֽל־ תִּשְׁפְּכ֖וּ בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For if you will indeed carry out these commands, then kings who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this palace riding on chariots and horses—they and their officials and their people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the king of Judah and his people.
The LORD gives commands to them.
If you obey these commands, good things will happen.
Kings from David’s family will come through the gates of this palace.
These kings will sit on David’s throne.
They will ride in chariots and on horses.
Their officials will come with them.
Their people will also come with them.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אִם־ עָשׂוֹ֙ תַּֽעֲשׂ֔וּ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה וּבָ֣אוּ בְשַׁעֲרֵ֣י הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֡ה מְלָכִים֩ יֹשְׁבִ֨ים לְדָוִ֜ד עַל־ כִּסְא֗וֹ רֹֽכְבִים֙ בָּרֶ֣כֶב וּבַסּוּסִ֔ים ה֥וּא וְעַבְדּוֹ וְעַמּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But if you do not obey these words, then I swear by Myself, declares the LORD, that this house will become a pile of rubble.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is speaking.
The LORD gives a warning.
If you do not obey these words, I will act.
I, the LORD, make this promise by Myself.
This house will become a pile of rubble.
passages.original: וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תִשְׁמְע֔וּ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה בִּ֤י נִשְׁבַּ֙עְתִּי֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּי־ לְחָרְבָּ֥ה יִֽהְיֶ֖ה הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says concerning the house of the king of Judah: “You are like Gilead to Me, like the summit of Lebanon; but I will surely turn you into a desert, like cities that are uninhabited.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the house of the king of Judah.
The LORD says, “You are precious to Me.
You are like Gilead to Me.
You are like the summit of Lebanon to Me.
But I will make you a desert.
You will become like cities where no one lives.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ כֹ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל־ בֵּית֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה גִּלְעָ֥ד אַתָּ֛ה לִ֖י רֹ֣אשׁ הַלְּבָנ֑וֹן אִם־ לֹ֤א אֲשִֽׁיתְךָ֙ מִדְבָּ֔ר עָרִ֖ים לֹ֥א נוֹשָׁבָה׃

passages.text: I will appoint destroyers against you, each man with his weapons, and they will cut down the choicest of your cedars and throw them into the fire.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the house of the king of Judah.
The LORD will appoint destroyers against you.
Each destroyer will come with his own weapons.
They will cut down your best cedar trees.
They will throw these trees into the fire.
passages.original: וְקִדַּשְׁתִּ֥י עָלֶ֛יךָ מַשְׁחִתִ֖ים אִ֣ישׁ וְכֵלָ֑יו וְכָֽרְתוּ֙ מִבְחַ֣ר אֲרָזֶ֔יךָ וְהִפִּ֖ילוּ עַל־ הָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: And many nations will pass by this city and ask one another, ‘Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?’
passages.sermon:
Many nations will pass by this city.
Each nation will see the city.
People from these nations will speak to each other.
They will ask, “Why did the LORD do this to this great city?”
passages.original: וְעָֽבְרוּ֙ גּוֹיִ֣ם רַבִּ֔ים עַ֖ל הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וְאָֽמְרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֔הוּ עַל־ מֶ֨ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כָּ֔כָה לָעִ֥יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: Then people will reply, ‘Because they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God and have worshiped and served other gods.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The people will answer a question about the city’s destruction.
They will say the people of the city abandoned the covenant.
The covenant is the agreement with the LORD, their God.
The people left the LORD, their God.
They bowed down to other gods.
They served these other gods.
passages.original: וְאָ֣מְר֔וּ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽזְב֔וּ אֶת־ בְּרִ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ לֵאלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים וַיַּעַבְדֽוּם׃ס

passages.text: Do not weep for the dead king; do not mourn his loss. Weep bitterly for the one who is exiled, for he will never return to see his native land.
passages.sermon:
Do not weep for the dead king.
Do not mourn for him.
Weep deeply for the one who is exiled.
He will never return.
He will never see his homeland again.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּבְכּ֣וּ לְמֵ֔ת וְאַל־ תָּנֻ֖דוּ ל֑וֹ בְּכ֤וּ בָכוֹ֙ לַֽהֹלֵ֔ךְ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָשׁוּב֙ ע֔וֹד וְרָאָ֖ה אֶת־ אֶ֥רֶץ מוֹלַדְתּֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the LORD says concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who succeeded his father Josiah but has gone forth from this place: “He will never return, but he will die in the place to which he was exiled; he will never see this land again.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke about Shallum.
Shallum was the son of Josiah.
Josiah was king of Judah.
Shallum became king after his father Josiah.
Shallum left this land.
The LORD said Shallum will never return here.
Shallum will die in the place where he was exiled.
He will never see this land again.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָֽמַר־ יְ֠הוָה אֶל־ שַׁלֻּ֨ם בֶּן־ יֹאשִׁיָּ֜הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה הַמֹּלֵךְ֙ תַּ֚חַת יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָצָ֖א מִן־ הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה לֹֽא־ יָשׁ֥וּב שָׁ֖ם עֽוֹד׃ כִּ֗י בִּמְק֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ הִגְל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ שָׁ֣ם יָמ֑וּת וְאֶת־ הָאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּ֖את לֹֽא־ יִרְאֶ֥ה עֽוֹד׃ס

passages.text: “Woe to him who builds his palace by unrighteousness, and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his countrymen serve without pay, and fails to pay their wages, who says, ‘I will build myself a great palace, with spacious upper rooms.’ So he cuts windows in it, panels it with cedar, and paints it with vermilion.
passages.sermon:
God warns those who act unjustly.
Woe to the person who builds his house without righteousness.
Woe to the person who makes his upper rooms without justice.
He forces his neighbor to work for nothing.
He does not pay his workers their wages.
He says, “I will build a large house for myself.”
He says, “I will make spacious upper rooms.”
He cuts windows for his house.
He covers it with cedar wood.
He paints it with bright red color.
passages.original: ה֣וֹי בֹּנֶ֤ה בֵיתוֹ֙ בְּֽלֹא־ צֶ֔דֶק וַעֲלִיּוֹתָ֖יו בְּלֹ֣א מִשְׁפָּ֑ט בְּרֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ יַעֲבֹ֣ד חִנָּ֔ם וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לֹ֥א יִתֶּן־ לֽוֹ׃ הָאֹמֵ֗ר אֶבְנֶה־ לִּי֙ בֵּ֣ית מִדּ֔וֹת וַעֲלִיּ֖וֹת מְרֻוָּחִ֑ים וְקָ֤רַֽע לוֹ֙ חַלּוֹנָ֔י וְסָפ֣וּן בָּאָ֔רֶז וּמָשׁ֖וֹחַ בַּשָּׁשַֽׁר׃

passages.text: Does it make you a king to excel in cedar? Did not your father have food and drink? He administered justice and righteousness, and so it went well with him.
passages.sermon:
This message is about the king of Judah, the son of Josiah.
You want to be a king because you build with fine cedar.
Building with cedar does not make you a true king.
Your father Josiah had food and drink.
Josiah did what was right and just.
Things went well for Josiah because he practiced justice and righteousness.
passages.original: הֲתִֽמְלֹ֔ךְ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה מְתַחֲרֶ֣ה בָאָ֑רֶז אָבִ֜יךָ הֲל֧וֹא אָכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֗ה וְעָשָׂ֤ה מִשְׁפָּט֙ וּצְדָקָ֔ה אָ֖ז ט֥וֹב לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He took up the cause of the poor and needy, and so it went well with him. Is this not what it means to know Me?” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God describes a king who ruled before.
This king defended the rights of the poor.
He also defended the rights of the needy.
Because of this, things went well for him.
God says, “To know Me means to do these things.”
This is what the LORD declares.
passages.original: דָּ֛ן דִּין־ עָנִ֥י וְאֶבְי֖וֹן אָ֣ז ט֑וֹב הֲלוֹא־ הִ֛יא הַדַּ֥עַת אֹתִ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “But your eyes and heart are set on nothing except your own dishonest gain, on shedding innocent blood, on practicing extortion and oppression.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jehoiakim, king of Judah.
God sees Jehoiakim’s actions and desires.
Jehoiakim’s eyes look only for his own profit.
Jehoiakim’s heart cares only for dishonest gain.
Jehoiakim seeks to shed innocent blood.
Jehoiakim practices extortion.
Jehoiakim commits acts of oppression.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין עֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ וְלִבְּךָ֔ כִּ֖י אִם־ עַל־ בִּצְעֶ֑ךָ וְעַ֤ל דַּֽם־ הַנָּקִי֙ לִשְׁפּ֔וֹךְ וְעַל־ הָעֹ֥שֶׁק וְעַל־ הַמְּרוּצָ֖ה לַעֲשֽׂוֹת׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: “They will not mourn for him: ‘Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!’ They will not mourn for him: ‘Alas, my master! Alas, his splendor!’
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about Jehoiakim.
Jehoiakim is the son of Josiah.
Jehoiakim is the king of Judah.
The LORD says Jehoiakim will die.
No one will mourn for Jehoiakim.
No one will say, “Alas, my brother!”
No one will say, “Alas, my sister!”
No one will say, “Alas, my master!”
No one will say, “Alas, his splendor!”
passages.original: לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־ יְהוֹיָקִ֤ים בֶּן־ יֹאשִׁיָּ֙הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹא־ יִסְפְּד֣וּ ל֔וֹ ה֥וֹי אָחִ֖י וְה֣וֹי אָח֑וֹת לֹא־ יִסְפְּד֣וּ ל֔וֹ ה֥וֹי אָד֖וֹן וְה֥וֹי הֹדֹֽה׃

passages.text: He will be buried like a donkey, dragged away and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Jehoiakim is the king of Judah.
God speaks about Jehoiakim.
Jehoiakim will not receive an honorable burial.
People will bury Jehoiakim like a donkey.
They will drag his body away.
They will throw his body outside the gates of Jerusalem.
passages.original: קְבוּרַ֥ת חֲמ֖וֹר יִקָּבֵ֑ר סָח֣וֹב וְהַשְׁלֵ֔ךְ מֵהָ֖לְאָה לְשַׁעֲרֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan; cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers have been crushed.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God commands them to go up to Lebanon.
God tells them to cry out there.
God tells them to raise their voice in Bashan.
God tells them to cry out from Abarim.
God says all their lovers have been crushed.
passages.original: עֲלִ֤י הַלְּבָנוֹן֙ וּֽצְעָ֔קִי וּבַבָּשָׁ֖ן תְּנִ֣י קוֹלֵ֑ךְ וְצַֽעֲקִי֙ מֵֽעֲבָרִ֔ים כִּ֥י נִשְׁבְּר֖וּ כָּל־ מְאַהֲבָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: I warned you when you were secure. You said, ‘I will not listen.’ This has been your way from youth, that you have not obeyed My voice.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to you when you were safe.
You answered, “I will not listen.”
You have acted this way since you were young.
You have never obeyed God’s voice.
passages.original: דִּבַּ֤רְתִּי אֵלַ֙יִךְ֙ בְּשַׁלְוֺתַ֔יִךְ אָמַ֖רְתְּ לֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֑ע זֶ֤ה דַרְכֵּךְ֙ מִנְּעוּרַ֔יִךְ כִּ֥י לֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֖עַתְּ בְּקוֹלִֽי׃

passages.text: The wind will drive away all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your wickedness.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God says their leaders are like shepherds.
The wind will scatter all their shepherds.
Their lovers will go into captivity.
The people will feel shame.
They will feel humiliation.
This will happen because of all their wickedness.
passages.original: כָּל־ רֹעַ֙יִךְ֙ תִּרְעֶה־ ר֔וּחַ וּֽמְאַהֲבַ֖יִךְ בַּשְּׁבִ֣י יֵלֵ֑כוּ כִּ֣י אָ֤ז תֵּבֹ֙שִׁי֙ וְנִכְלַ֔מְתְּ מִכֹּ֖ל רָעָתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: O inhabitant of Lebanon, nestled in the cedars, how you will groan when pangs of anguish come upon you, agony like a woman in labor.”
passages.sermon:
You live in Lebanon.
You rest among the cedar trees.
You feel safe and secure there.
But trouble will come to you.
You will groan in pain.
You will suffer like a woman giving birth.
Your anguish will be great.
passages.original: יֹשַׁבְתִּי בַּלְּבָנ֔וֹן מְקֻנַּנְתִּי בָּֽאֲרָזִ֑ים מַה־ נֵּחַנְתְּ֙ בְּבֹא־ לָ֣ךְ חֲבָלִ֔ים חִ֖יל כַּיֹּלֵדָֽה׃

passages.text: “As surely as I live,” declares the LORD, “even if you, Coniah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, were a signet ring on My right hand, I would pull you off.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD lives forever.
The LORD makes a promise.
Coniah is the son of Jehoiakim.
Coniah is king of Judah.
The LORD addresses Coniah directly.
A signet ring is precious and close to its owner.
The LORD says, “Even if you, Coniah, were a signet ring on My right hand, I would pull you off.”
passages.original: חַי־ אָנִי֮ נְאֻם־ יְהוָה֒ כִּ֣י אִם־ יִהְיֶ֞ה כָּנְיָ֤הוּ בֶן־ יְהֽוֹיָקִים֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה חוֹתָ֖ם עַל־ יַ֣ד יְמִינִ֑י כִּ֥י מִשָּׁ֖ם אֶתְּקֶֽנְךָּ׃

passages.text: In fact, I will hand you over to those you dread, who want to take your life—to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Coniah, son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah.
God says, “I will hand you over.
I will give you to those who want to take your life.
You fear these people.
I will give you to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
I will give you to the Chaldeans.
passages.original: וּנְתַתִּ֗יךָ בְּיַד֙ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וּבְיַ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־ אַתָּ֥ה יָג֖וֹר מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וּבְיַ֛ד נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל וּבְיַ֥ד הַכַּשְׂדִּֽים׃

passages.text: I will hurl you and the mother who gave you birth into another land, where neither of you were born—and there you both will die.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Coniah, son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah.
Coniah is the subject.
The LORD will act.
The LORD will throw Coniah into another land.
The LORD will also throw Coniah’s mother into that land.
Coniah’s mother gave birth to him.
This land is not the place where Coniah or his mother were born.
Coniah and his mother will die in that foreign land.
passages.original: וְהֵֽטַלְתִּ֣י אֹתְךָ֗ וְאֶֽת־ אִמְּךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְלָדַ֔תְךָ עַ֚ל הָאָ֣רֶץ אַחֶ֔רֶת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ יֻלַּדְתֶּ֖ם שָׁ֑ם וְשָׁ֖ם תָּמֽוּתוּ׃

passages.text: You will never return to the land for which you long.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Coniah and his people.
They long to return to their homeland.
They desire to go back to the land of Judah.
God says they will not return there.
They will never go back to the land they miss.
passages.original: וְעַל־ הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ הֵ֛ם מְנַשְּׂאִ֥ים אֶת־ נַפְשָׁ֖ם לָשׁ֣וּב שָׁ֑ם שָׁ֖מָּה לֹ֥א יָשֽׁוּבוּ׃ס

passages.text: Is this man Coniah a despised and shattered pot, a jar that no one wants? Why are he and his descendants hurled out and cast into a land they do not know?
passages.sermon:
Coniah is a man.
People see Coniah as worthless.
People see Coniah as broken.
People do not want Coniah.
Coniah is like a shattered pot.
Coniah is like a jar that no one wants.
People throw out Coniah.
People throw out his descendants.
They cast them into a land they do not know.
passages.original: הַעֶ֨צֶב נִבְזֶ֜ה נָפ֗וּץ הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ כָּנְיָ֔הוּ אִ֨ם־ כְּלִ֔י אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ בּ֑וֹ מַדּ֤וּעַ הֽוּטֲלוּ֙ ה֣וּא וְזַרְע֔וֹ וְהֻ֨שְׁלְכ֔וּ עַל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ יָדָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: O land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the land.
The LORD commands the land to listen.
The LORD says, "Land, hear My word."
The LORD repeats, "Land, land, land, listen to Me."
The LORD wants the land to obey His word.
passages.original: אֶ֥רֶץ אֶ֖רֶץ אָ֑רֶץ שִׁמְעִ֖י דְּבַר־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Enroll this man as childless, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime. None of his descendants will prosper to sit on the throne of David or to rule again in Judah.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD gives a command.
Write down a judgment about this man.
This man is Coniah.
Coniah is to be recorded as childless.
Coniah will not succeed during his life.
None of Coniah’s descendants will succeed.
No descendant of Coniah will sit on David’s throne.
No descendant of Coniah will rule again in Judah.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה כִּתְב֞וּ אֶת־ הָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ עֲרִירִ֔י גֶּ֖בֶר לֹא־ יִצְלַ֣ח בְּיָמָ֑יו כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יִצְלַ֜ח מִזַּרְע֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ יֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־ כִּסֵּ֣א דָוִ֔ד וּמֹשֵׁ֥ל ע֖וֹד בִּיהוּדָֽה׃
